nodes.text: Let $a_1<a_2<\cdots$ be an increasing sequence such that $a_n/n\to \infty$. Is the sum\[\sum_n \frac{a_n}{2^{a_n}}\]irrational?

#260 : [Er74b] [ErGr80] [Er81h,p.180] [Er88c,p.103] [Va99,1.33] irrationality Erdős [Er81l] proved this is true under either of the stronger assumptions that $a_{n+1}-a_n\to \infty$ or $a_n \gg n\sqrt{\log n\log\log n}$. Erdős and Graham speculate that the condition $\limsup a_{n+1}-a_n=\infty$ is not sufficient, but know of no example. In [Va99] this is asked with $a_n/n\to \infty$ replaced by $a_{n+1}-a_n\to \infty$, which as above was proved by Erdős in [Er81l] .
